entry.reasons: The entry accurately represents the formula and concept described in Essential Knowledge 9.3.A.1, which states that the change in electric potential energy of the object-field system is given by an equation when a charged object moves through a potential difference. The caution correctly highlights the system-based nature of potential energy as emphasized in the CED ('object-field system').

Topic 9.3.A.1 requires the change in electric potential energy when a charged object moves between locations with different electric potentials. The formula ΔU_E = qΔV agrees with that relationship and with 9.2.A.3, which defines potential difference as the change in electric potential energy per unit charge. The caution correctly preserves 9.3.A.1’s wording: the energy is that of the “object-field system.”

a_factual: 9.3.A.1 states that when a charged object moves between locations with different electric potentials, 'the resulting change in the electric potential energy of the object-field system is given by the following equation.' The equation image did not survive text extraction, so the symbols are checked against the physics the CED states. ΔU_E = qΔV is consistent with 9.2.A.3, which defines potential difference as 'the change in electric potential energy per unit charge.' b_topic_codes: 9.3 is the topic where the CED requires this relation (9.3.A.1), and the entry's topic_codes list contains only 9.3, which is correct. Topic 9.2 uses ΔV in its definitions, but the ΔU = qΔV statement itself is required under 9.3. c_ced_required: learning objective 9.3.A ('Describe changes in a system due to a difference in electric potential between two locations') and essential knowledge 9.3.A.1 require students to apply this equation. d_caution: the CED wording is 'change in the electric potential energy of the object-field system,' and the entry title says 'Change in potential energy of a charge.' The caution ('belongs to the object-field system, not to the charge alone (9.3.A.1)') corrects that wording and cites the right statement, so it is present and needed.
